# Compute Engine

**Parity grade: B** · SDK `cloud.google.com/go/compute@v1.72.0` · last audited 2026-10-26 (`cf047c847`)

## Coverage

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Feature families | 8 (5 ok, 2 partial, 1 gap) |
| Known gaps | 10 |
| Deferred items | 0 |
| Resource leaks | unknown |

### Known gaps

- Load balancing: target pools, target instances, service attachments, legacy HTTP health checks, regional SSL policies, regional TCP/SSL certificates managed by Certificate Manager, certificate maps, backend service patch fields such as outlier detection are stored without effect, urlMaps.invalidateCache and forwardingRules.patch are not routed, and managed certificates never leave PROVISIONING. No traffic is forwarded and nothing is probed (see BackendServices.GetHealth). Backend bucket existence is not checked against gcpstorage. Cloud Armor security policies are state only: there is no HTTP load balancer data plane, so SRC_IPS_V1 and CEL rules are never evaluated and nothing is allowed or denied; aggregatedList, listPreconfiguredExpressionSets, regional and organization policies, associations, edge/backend bucket attachment and adaptive protection behaviour are not modelled.
- Instance groups: utilization-based autoscaling has no metric source; stateful policy, per-instance configs, resize requests, createInstances, start/stop/suspend/resume instances, listErrors and instanceFlexibilityPolicy are not implemented; instance creation errors fail the whole call instead of surfacing as group errors; autohealing probes only reach instances that carry the gopherstack-health-endpoint metadata key (no guest network exists), and gRPC checks are a TCP connect.
- Instance templates from sourceInstance in another project are 404-class unsupported, DEFAULT disk instantiation does not create a custom image, and regional-only fields beyond the stored properties are not modelled; GRPC_WITH_TLS health checks and regional composite health checks are not modelled.
- VPN gateways/tunnels, interconnects, shared VPC, licenses, instant snapshot groups, regional disk async replication and policies, machine image encryption and future/aggregate reservations are not routed (404). Network peering has no CONSENSUS update strategy, requestRemovePeering or cancelRequestRemovePeering, stores the public-IP subnet route flags without effect (all emulator subnets are private or special-use ranges), and peer networks must exist in the emulator; peering routes are not added to routes.list. Resource policies are state only: schedules never take snapshots or start/stop instances, resourceStatus.instanceSchedulePolicy run times are not computed and status never becomes EXPIRED.
- Instances: local SSD (SCRATCH) disks, GPUs at insert, IPv6 and alias IP ranges at insert are rejected or stored without effect (updateNetworkInterface stores alias ranges). instances.update uses a modelled field classification (see Instances.Update); getSerialPortOutput returns empty output and getGuestAttributes is always 404 because no guest runs.
- Routes cannot use VPN tunnel, ILB, hub, peering or network next hops, and there are no dynamic (BGP) routes. The default-route-<hash> name is derived from the subnetwork self link rather than random; the real hash input is unknown.
- Regional IPv6 addresses, internal IPv6, PRIVATE_SERVICE_CONNECT and other global INTERNAL purposes, and prefix-length reservations other than VPC_PEERING and global IPv6 are rejected.
- Error message texts for state conflicts (resourceNotReady on setMachineType/reset/detach/suspend/resume/setScheduling), peering overlap and duplicate errors, subnet route delete, resourceInUseByAnotherResource wording, required-field and validation messages, and the firewall rule for ingress without sources were chosen without a production reference.
- Only a fixed set of 15 regions, 46 zones, 9 image families, e2/n2/n1-standard machine types and 3 persistent disk types exist; image point releases are pinned, region quotas and Project usage quotas are not modelled, and the status/progress timing is a fixed model.
- The emulator does not enforce IAM or return permission errors.
